gaps.summary: Trusted-entry-seeded snes2asm comparison now covers 20 directly comparable executable subregions with 1,455 aligned opcode positions. All aligned opcode bytes, opcode/operand roles, and M/X states agree; 510 aligned byte changes are operand bytes. Checkpoint/finish additionally contains one explicit structural delta: Europe retail contracts USA 81:8102..8117 (22-byte frame-normalization logic) to 81:8102..8109 (8 bytes), a net -14 bytes. USA retail, legacy beta, and the 1994-11-29 PAL prototype retain the 22-byte executable shape; Europe retail alone uses the contracted form. A parallel USA/PAL-prototype pass covers 19 trusted subregions with 1,465 aligned opcode positions: zero opcode substitutions, zero role/MX disagreements, and 296 operand-byte changes. This confirms the prototype preserves the USA executable stream throughout the tested corpus and is materially closer to USA than Europe retail at the operand/layout level.
gaps.next_evidence: Trusted code-shape comparisons are saturated. Remaining high-information comparative work is WRAM lineage: identify the Europe-only state responsible for the +4 insertion after 0309/before old 030D and the +2 insertion after 053B/before old 0541. Do not broaden analyzer coverage absent a new disagreement.

gaps.region: Europe-retail WRAM insertion brackets after 0309/before old 030D and after 053B/before old 0541
gaps.summary: Cross-build operand motion proves two post-1994-11-29 Europe-retail WRAM expansions: +4 bytes after stable 0309/before the relocated controller buffer at old 030D, and +2 bytes after 053B/before old 0541. An all-trusted-anchor scan finds no unexplained direct Europe operands in either inserted span. Europe auto-joypad capture still reads only 4218..421B and stores the same four-byte payload at relocated 0311..0314, so the first insertion is not extra controller capture state.
gaps.next_evidence: Only pursue exact inserted-field semantics via indexed/indirect access reconstruction, runtime watchpoints, or newly recovered source/comments. Direct absolute-reference mining is currently exhausted.
